items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: So I go to Mel Williams.

ctx.x:

One of the first artists to play on White jukeboxes, in White joints, was Louis Jordan. After Louis Jordan, then came King Cole. When he made "Nature Boy," you found him in every hotel in the country. You would hear... He's the one that revolutionized this thing where you can hear Black artists on White... Because some jukebox owners didn't have a record... I knew some of them, because I approached them with my record. They had never had a Black record in the store. Everything was…

All right. So I go to Mel Williams. So he said, "Well, would you..." He looked at Lu and said, "Yes, you can sing, but we need something more." So he said, "Think of something raunchy, and come back." So I get back home, and I think "What was that thing that my mother used to sing, 'When you feel my leg'..." "When you feel my leg..." I said, "What else?" She used to sing, "When you feel my leg, when you feel my thighs..." I don't know where my mother got that from. It's (?) original, because I never heard nobody…
